title: Existing-position exit rules follow-ups — further-further non-blocking review follow-up
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #49 (portfolio-exit-rules-followups-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: protective_stop()'s new `columns_validated: bool = False` parameter (backend/app/portfolio/risk.py) is only exercised indirectly: no test in backend/tests/unit/test_portfolio_risk.py calls protective_stop() directly with columns_validated=True to confirm, in isolation, that it genuinely skips the {'low', 'close'} column-membership check (as opposed to that skip only ever being safe in practice because evaluate_exit_flags -- the sole caller that passes it -- always hands it an already-column-valid frame). Coverage on risk.py is 100% branch, satisfied entirely via evaluate_exit_flags's own end-to-end tests (e.g. test_real_too_short_daily_history_raises exercises the columns_validated=True + empty-frame branch). Worth adding a direct unit test next time risk.py is touched -- e.g. protective_stop(position, a frame missing 'low' but non-empty, columns_validated=True) either raises a KeyError (documenting the parameter's real contract: it trusts the caller, it doesn't re-check) or is asserted not to raise the 'missing required column(s)' ValueError -- so the parameter's own skip-semantics has regression coverage independent of any particular caller's usage pattern.
